```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 06_probability_pair_of_dice
title: >
  Counting with two dice
questions:
  - id: sum_nine
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      Using the table of 36 equally likely outcomes, what is the probability of rolling a sum
      of 9? Enter a decimal, rounded to at least two decimal places.
    hint: >
      Count the cells containing a 9. Remember that a 4 on the first die and a 5
      on the second is a different outcome from a 5 on the first die and a 4 on
      the second.
    answer: 0.1111
    tolerance: 0.005
    explanation: >
      There are four ways to make a 9 — (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), and (6,3) — out of
      36 equally likely outcomes, so $P(9) = 4/36 \approx .11$.
  - id: corner_three_eight_ten
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      The Catan board earlier had an intersection that touches tiles numbered 3, 8,
      and 10. What is the probability that it earns resources on a given
      roll? Enter a decimal, rounded to at least two decimal places.
    hint: >
      A single roll cannot be two different sums at once, so no outcome gets
      counted twice. Add up the ways.
    answer: 0.2778
    tolerance: 0.005
    explanation: >
      There are two ways to roll a 3, five ways to roll an 8, and three ways to
      roll a 10, and no outcome is more than one of them, so
      $P(3 \text{ or } 8 \text{ or } 10) = (2 + 5 + 3)/36 = 10/36 \approx .28$.
```
